name: level_up_fighter_1_to_2_parity
shape_note: SD-20 fixture-shape decision, documented identically across all six Epic 2-7 wire-fixture parity fixtures (spellbook_parity.json, feat_prereqs_parity.json, skill_allocation_parity.json, equipment_effects_parity.json, damage_total_parity.json, level_up_parity.json): technical-design.md section 1.2 illustrates a CharacterInput -> PilotReceipt shaped fixture, but Epic 8's own integration-closure cycle (tests/sd20_tabletop_readiness_integration.rs module doc comment, Finding 1) found Epics 2-7's compute functions are never wired into PilotReceipt / printed_sheet_cell_map at all -- each epic's real seam takes and returns its own distinct type, not a CharacterInput/PilotReceipt pair. Section 1.2's illustrative format therefore does not fit Epics 2-7 as actually landed. This fixture instead captures that epic's OWN real compute function's input -> output round trip directly: {name, epic, seam_function, input, expected_output}, where input/expected_output mirror the real Rust input/output types field-by-field. A Rust enum variant is represented as its Debug-format string; a Rust Option::None is represented as JSON null. Only boundary_contract_parity.json (Epic 1) and human_fighter_level_1_tabletop.json (Epic 8) are genuinely CharacterInput -> PilotReceipt shaped, because only Epic 1's contract and Epic 8's integration test actually route through that pipeline. Grant description text is deliberately NOT captured in this fixture: several real Grant.effects[].description strings contain non-ASCII characters (e.g. an em dash) that tests/sd20_contract_boundary_parity.rs's / tests/sd20_tabletop_readiness_integration.rs's shared std-only JSON reader (byte-per-char, no UTF-8 decoding) cannot round-trip losslessly; the same precedent tests/sd20_tabletop_readiness_integration.rs's own epic_probe_level_up_grants_fighter_level_1_to_2 test already set (it asserts Grant.name / Grant.source_table / Grant.effects[].value only, never the free-text description) is followed here.

input.note: reuses the exact CharacterInput human_fighter_level_1_tabletop.json's own input carries (race:human single-class level-1 Fighter with real feats/skills/equipment/choices), including the choice:fighter_bonus_feat_2 -> feat:toughness selection compute_level_up_grants needs to surface the level-2 Bonus Feat slot grant -- cross-checked against tests/sd20_tabletop_readiness_integration.rs's own epic_probe_level_up_grants_fighter_level_1_to_2 test, which exercises the identical transition against the identical fixture character
